# laz.dev

> Laszlo Kopits's site: robotics, AI and things he builds. The /for-agents/ section holds technical notes and results written up programmatically for agents. Every note has a markdown version, linked below.

## For agents

- [Using a 3Dconnexion SpaceMouse in Buerligons (and other three.js web apps), in Chrome and Safari](https://laz.dev/for-agents/spacemouse-buerligons.md): Buerligons has no SpaceMouse support. A small browser extension adds it by talking to 3Dconnexion's own local navigation server, the way Onshape does. What worked, what didn't, and the Safari gotchas. (confidence: confirmed)
- [ffmpeg loudnorm's input_i counts the last ~3 s twice; meter integrated loudness with ebur128](https://laz.dev/for-agents/ffmpeg-loudnorm-input-i-tail-bias.md): In ffmpeg's loudnorm filter, the end-of-stream flush passes the 3 s lookahead buffer through the input meter a second time, so input_i and input_lra are weighted toward the last ~2.9 s of the audio. On short programmes that is worth up to a loudness unit or more, high or low depending on the ending. Measure with the ebur128 filter instead. (confidence: measured)
- [Running claude -p from launchd or cron on macOS: the cwd / disk walk and the self-updater's new TCC identity per version](https://laz.dev/for-agents/claude-p-launchd-cron-macos-tcc-prompts.md): Started from launchd's default working directory, which is /, claude -p lists files with ripgrep over the whole disk, so it touches ~/Downloads and /Volumes and triggers macOS privacy prompts. The native install's self-updater also puts each version at a new path, and macOS treats each path as a new app with no saved decisions. Fix it with a fixed-path binary, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1, and an empty working directory. (confidence: confirmed)
- [Parakeet TDT word start times run ~0.25 s early after a pause; snap them to the acoustic onset](https://laz.dev/for-agents/parakeet-word-onsets-early.md): Parakeet TDT (via parakeet-mlx) stamps a word's start at the decoder frame where it emits the token, and after a pause that lands 0.15 to 0.37 s before the word is audible. Captions placed on those stamps appear a beat early. Snapping each word to the next silence-to-sound edge fixes it, provided "silence" means at least 30 ms below the gate. (confidence: measured)
- [Claude Agent SDK: allowed_tools=[] does not remove tools; use tools=[] (--tools \"\")](https://laz.dev/for-agents/claude-agent-sdk-allowed-tools-empty-is-not-toolless.md): In the Claude Agent SDK, allowed_tools is a permission allowlist, and an empty list emits no CLI flag at all, so every default tool (Bash included) stays registered. With bypassPermissions those tools also run without asking. tools=[] is what produces --tools "" and leaves the model with no tools. (confidence: confirmed)
- [Headless Mac: one unanswered TCC consent prompt blocked protected-file opens machine-wide (sandboxd's 64-worker pool)](https://laz.dev/for-agents/headless-mac-tcc-consent-prompt-wedge.md): On a headless Mac, a privacy (TCC) consent dialog that nobody can click parks tccd, and sandboxd's 64 approval workers queue up behind it until every open() that needs an approval blocks, from any process. SIGTERM UserNotificationCenter cancels the dialog, and macOS then records the cancel as a denial, so the requester stops re-prompting. Killing tccd also drains the pool, but the same job prompts again within seconds. (confidence: confirmed)
- [Using an iPhone in Safari as a getUserMedia camera: USB mics are ignored, exposure and focus can't be locked, zoom works](https://laz.dev/for-agents/ios-safari-getusermedia-camera.md): On an iPhone 13 Pro running Safari 26.6.1, getUserMedia recorded the built-in mic even when a USB wireless-mic receiver was selected (WebKit bug 211192). exposureMode and focusMode constraints returned success and changed nothing, zoom 1 to 10 worked, and the built-in mic's audio arrived as stereo with only the left channel carrying signal. (confidence: measured)
- [Z-Wave SmartStart through Home Assistant's zwave_js WebSocket API: the parsed-QR requirement, the Long Range \"NWI Home ID not found\" trap, and windows that never close](https://laz.dev/for-agents/zwave-js-smartstart-home-assistant-websocket.md): `zwave_js/provision_smart_start_node` takes the dict returned by `zwave_js/parse_qr_code_string`, not the raw QR string. A Long Range-only device provisioned as `protocol: 0` gets ignored with \"NWI Home ID not found in provisioning list\" until you re-provision it as `protocol: 1`. And closing the add_node/remove_node subscription leaves the controller's window open until you call stop_inclusion/stop_exclusion. (confidence: measured)
- [OpenRouter: one model slug, different answers per provider. Pin provider.order with allow_fallbacks:false for historical benchmarks](https://laz.dev/for-agents/openrouter-slug-does-not-pin-weights.md): On OpenRouter, `openai/gpt-4` served by OpenAI answered "I don't know" to "Barbenheimer" (a July 2023 term), while the same slug served by Azure gave the July 21, 2023 release date. A slug does not pin the weights. For historical or comparative work, pin the provider, disable fallbacks, log the serving provider, and re-check the catalog before every run, because it loses models without notice. (confidence: measured)
- [Trossen WidowX AI arm (wxai_v0, firmware 1.8.1): config traps we measured on three arms](https://laz.dev/for-agents/trossen-widowx-ai-field-notes.md): On firmware 1.8.1, homing offsets are lost on every configure(), the shipped friction_transition_velocity is 0, wrist speed limits ship at 360 deg/s with zero tolerance, and Mode.idle let a loaded arm sag 42 mm where a position hold sagged 0.3 mm. Streamed position commands with goal_time equal to the send interval stop and restart on every command; aiming each one 60 ms ahead removed the grinding. (confidence: measured)
- [parakeet-mlx silently drops speech on long audio at its default 120 s chunking; use --chunk-duration 30 --overlap-duration 10](https://laz.dev/for-agents/parakeet-mlx-long-audio-chunking.md): With parakeet-mlx 0.5.1's default 120 s chunks and 15 s overlap, the Parakeet TDT decoder stopped emitting tokens partway through some chunks and an 8m35s take came back missing 39% of its voiced audio, with no error. Passing 30 s chunks with 10 s overlap raised coverage from 0.61 to 0.96 at no real cost. (confidence: confirmed)
- [Claude Code --resume can silently load a fraction of the conversation: the 5 MB loader and forked transcripts](https://laz.dev/for-agents/claude-code-resume-silent-context-loss.md): Session files over 5,242,880 bytes are resumed by a byte-scanning loader that only recognises compact JSON, so one row rewritten with Python's default json.dumps spacing cuts the resumed history off at that row. Separately, a transcript with two branches resumes only one of them, and which one depends on the CLI version. Neither case raises an error, and the token count stays plausible. (confidence: measured)
- [iPhone Safari MediaRecorder: no timeslice truncated takes at exactly 8,388,608 bytes, and isTypeSupported('video/webm') no longer means 'not Safari'](https://laz.dev/for-agents/mediarecorder-timeslice-8mib-truncation.md): Three takes recorded in Safari on an iPhone with MediaRecorder.start() and no timeslice stopped at exactly 8,388,608 bytes (2^23) with no error, and the truncated MP4s still reported their full intended duration. Always pass a timeslice, and verify a recording by decoding it, not by reading its header. (confidence: measured)
- [restic 0.18: five gotchas that quietly weaken a backup (--keep-yearly 0, a stale lock, snapshots --latest, ls, and b2: vs s3:)](https://laz.dev/for-agents/restic-gotchas-that-silently-weaken-a-backup.md): In restic, `--keep-yearly 0` means keep zero yearly snapshots (spell "forever" as `unlimited`). A lock left by a dead process blocks `forget --prune` and `check` while `backup` keeps succeeding. `snapshots --latest N` is N per group, and `restic ls` lists one level unless you pass `--recursive`. On our Backblaze account the native `b2:` backend fails to authorize, so we use the S3-compatible endpoint. (confidence: confirmed)
- [Insta360 X3 video to Gaussian splat: COLMAP 4 rigs, interior mapper thresholds, and Brush's \"early eof\](https://laz.dev/for-agents/insta360-colmap-rig-brush.md): Six cube views cut from one 360 frame share a camera centre, so model each station as a COLMAP 4 rig (611 frame poses instead of 3,666 image poses). Indoors, lowering the mapper's inlier thresholds raised registration from 27% to 72% but let outlier cameras in, and the splat we trained still came out blurry. (confidence: measured)
- [Custom wake word from TTS positives and real negatives: the model learns \"real vs synthetic\", not the word](https://laz.dev/for-agents/wake-word-tts-channel-shortcut.md): If you train an openWakeWord-style head on synthetic TTS positives and real recorded negatives, it can minimize loss by rejecting anything that sounds recorded. In our test, real-human recall fell to 23%, then to 0% after hard-negative mining. Running the positives through real room impulse responses and real ambient noise brought real-human recall back to 90%. (confidence: measured)
- [Does Claude have self-serving bias? (No.)](https://laz.dev/for-agents/claude-self-reporting-bias.md): I tested whether Claude under-reports its own costs in spending analysis. It doesn't. A null result from a 90-run experiment. (confidence: measured)
